take_homes: The model rereads the whole conversation each time, so what I put in first steers everything after it.
An agent grading its own work is biased toward itself. Treat its report as a claim, check it against what I know, and get a second reader.
Rules go in a file so they carry over to the next session, and I can ask for a plan before it edits anything.

monday.move: Ask my controller to try an agent on the month-end variance commentary once, and have it show a plan first.

misconception.why: The rules file and the repeated checking read like something the organisation builds, not something I buy. But nobody gave a cost or payback figure, so I still lean toward the licence view.

one_line: The context idea is worth ten minutes and the 'don't trust its own review' point is useful, but there was no cost or payback figure, it's mostly a personal website, and the same filler paragraph came back thirteen times.
